2J.3 We are exhorted to worship and serve only God.

precepts.text: The rock of our salvation is Christ. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand: to day if ye will hear his voice. The same thing Christ said in John 10: they shall hear my voice.
precepts.point: For all of us, there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God and it triggered us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Everything Christ and the apostles spoke was already spoken in what we call the Old Testament, and they used it to substantiate their points. So when Christ says of his other sheep, “they shall hear my voice”, the psalm already said it.

“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” The rock of our salvation is Christ. “For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth”; “The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.”

“For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice.” We are the sheep of his hand, and the condition is the same: if you will hear his voice. That is exactly what Christ said in John 10: “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice.”

For all of us there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God, and it brought us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life. That is how the sheep of his pasture are known.

precepts.text: That rock that followed them was Christ; the rock of our salvation is Christ.
precepts.point: Why should we make a joyful noise? Because at one time we thought Christ was white, we thought Christ was for everyone, and we were deceived by the nations. Knowing that Christ looked like us and He is a black man from the tribe of Judah is a joyful thing, and He is coming to save us, the so-called black, Hispanic, and native Indians. The rock, our foundation that we build this church and our faith upon, is Christ.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” Who is the rock of our salvation? Paul says our fathers in the wilderness “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

That rock that followed them was Christ, and the rock of our salvation is Christ. He is the rock, our foundation that we build this church and our faith upon.

Why should we make a joyful noise? Because at one time we thought Christ was white, we thought Christ was for everyone, and we were deceived by the nations. Knowing that Christ looked like us and he is a black man from the tribe of Judah is a joyful thing, and he is coming to save us, the so-called black, Hispanic and native Indians. So we should always be giving praise that you are an Israelite, the best people upon this earth above all nations.

precepts.text: God called the dry land earth; through the Lord's hand He made all things.
precepts.point: The sea is His, He made it, and His hands formed the dry land. Through the Lord's hand He made all things.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.” Genesis shows the day he did it: “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.”

God called the dry land Earth and the gathering together of the waters Seas. Through the Lord's hand he made all things. The sea is his because he made it, and the dry land is his because his hands formed it, along with the deep places of the earth and the strength of the hills, the strength being their height.

precepts.text: He made His own people go forth like sheep and guided them like a flock; we are that flock.
precepts.point: We are that flock, the lost sheep that needs to be found by the voice, this Bible. This Bible tells us from Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 who the Israelites are that have been scattered to the four corners of the earth. That is the gospel that needs to go out to give our people praise and uplift them in their spirits.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.” Psalm 78 shows when he made us his flock: he “made his own people to go forth like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.”

He made his own people go forth like sheep and guided them like a flock. We are that flock, the lost sheep that needs to be found by the voice, and that voice is this Bible. It tells us from Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 who the Israelites are that have been scattered to the four corners of the earth.

That is the gospel that needs to go out to give our people praise and uplift them in their spirits: he is our God, we are the sheep of his hand, and today if we will hear his voice.

precepts.text: Fear not little flock, it is the Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom; the kingdom is going to that flock, the Israelites.
precepts.point: We are that flock, the lost sheep that needs to be found by the voice, this Bible. This Bible tells us from Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 who the Israelites are that have been scattered to the four corners of the earth. That is the gospel that needs to go out to give our people praise and uplift them in their spirits.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
We are “the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand”, and Christ speaks to that same flock: “Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.”

Fear not, little flock; it is the Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. The kingdom is going to that flock, the Israelites, the sheep of his hand scattered to the four corners of the earth.

That is why the voice of this Bible needs to reach our people today: to tell the lost sheep who they are, to give them praise and uplift them in their spirits, because the kingdom belongs to the little flock.

precepts.text: These things were examples so we should not lust, be idolaters, commit fornication, tempt Christ, or murmur as our forefathers did; they are written for our admonition upon whom the ends of the world are come.
precepts.point: When your fathers tempted Me, proved Me, and saw My work. Now we are getting some history of our forefathers, but Paul told us the same thing in the New Testament: do not harden your heart, do not be like our forefathers.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
Paul gives the same warning David gives here, and he points to the same forefathers. “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” What our fathers did in the wilderness, when they tempted the Most High and proved him, was written down so that we would not do it.

Paul lists what they did: they were idolaters, for “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play”; they committed fornication, and “fell in one day three and twenty thousand”; they tempted Christ, “and were destroyed of serpents”; and they murmured, “and were destroyed of the destroyer.” Every one of those is a hardened heart, a mind provoked to sin.

“Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” We are the ones upon whom the ends of the world are come, so the history of our forefathers in Psalm 95 is our admonition: harden not your heart, do not be like them.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.
precepts.point: When your fathers tempted Me, proved Me, and saw My work. Now we are getting some history of our forefathers, but Paul told us the same thing in the New Testament: do not harden your heart, do not be like our forefathers.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The history of our fathers tempting the Most High in the wilderness is one of those things written aforetime. It is not there for a story; it is there for our learning.

So when Psalm 95 brings up the provocation and the day of temptation in the wilderness, we take it the way Paul tells us to: learn from it, do not harden your mind to sin as they did, and through the patience and comfort of the scriptures have hope.
